subject.title: perf(ci): cut the pre-fan-out critical path and bin canonical main runs

question: Should this maintainer-labeled CI scheduling change merge with static guard coverage plus monitoring of the first canonical-main run, or should it wait for an explicit canonical-main-equivalent runtime artifact?
rationale: The changed conditions are intentionally specific to pushes on the canonical main branch, while normal PR and workflow-dispatch paths do not directly exercise that topology; accepting a substitute for live proof is therefore a CI-owner judgment.

options.title: Approve controlled proof override
options.body: Accept the focused guards and green CI, rebase the branch, and monitor the first merged canonical-main run for debounce, cancellation, and bin-plan behavior.

options.title: Require pre-merge runtime evidence
options.body: Keep the PR open until a CI owner can provide a redacted artifact or transcript from a run that exercises the canonical-main scheduling conditions.

options.title: Pause the optimization
options.body: Defer the topology change if neither monitored rollout nor an equivalent proof path is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Approve controlled proof override
recommendation.body: Accept the focused guards and green CI, rebase the branch, and monitor the first merged canonical-main run for debounce, cancellation, and bin-plan behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: RomneyDa is the only evidence-backed historical owner supplied for the touched runtime-test surface; CI workflow ownership is otherwise not identifiable from the available provenance.
